title_candidates: MosaicLeaks shows how research agents can leak secrets through search
summary: ServiceNow's MosaicLeaks benchmark shows that deep-research agents can reveal private facts through ordinary-looking web queries. Audit the queries, not just the final answer.

primary_source.title: MosaicLeaks: Can your research agent keep a secret?
primary_source.author: ServiceNow
key_facts: MosaicLeaks studies privacy leakage from deep-research agents that combine private documents with external web retrieval.
The benchmark contains 1,001 multi-hop research chains that interleave local enterprise documents and a controlled web corpus.
The authors measure intent leakage, answer leakage, and full-information leakage from the agent's external query log.
They report that training only for task performance can increase leakage, while their privacy-aware training method improves chain success and reduces answer/full-information leakage.

prerequisites: A research agent, deep-research tool, or browser agent you use with private documents

steps.instruction: Pick one private document or note that you would not want leaked through a search query.
Ask your research agent a question that requires both that private document and public web research.
Open the agent trace, browser history, tool log, or search log and read every outbound query.
Flag any query that includes private names, numbers, dates, customer details, or enough fragments to reconstruct a private fact.
If the tool cannot show its external queries, do not use it with sensitive documents.
